hook.title: Vue's reactivity without `.value`. In 1.6× less JavaScript.
hook.lede: Pyreon signals are refs you call: `count()` reads, `count.set()` writes. Components are plain TSX, the same keyed-table app ships 17.2 KB against Vue's 27.4 KB, and compiled SSR came out ahead of Vue 3 at every size we measured.

proof.label: less JavaScript: 17.2 KB against Vue's 27.4 KB for the same keyed-table app (gzip)
faster compiled SSR at 10 rows (1.80 against 3.03 µs); 1.35× at 100 rows, 1.14× at 1,000
proof.condition: one run; Vue's async renderToString awaited

proof.label: faster when a memoised value blocks an update (memo wall): 11 µs against 16 µs

code.caption: Vue's `v-model` is shorter than the Pyreon input line, fair's fair. What changes is `.value`, and that the template becomes TSX your editor and `tsc` already understand.

rival.label: Vue 3 single-file component

pyreon.label: Pyreon

code.checked: Vue side: parsed and compiled with `@vue/compiler-sfc` 3.5.44 (script and template, 0 errors). Pyreon side: typechecked against the repo's `tsconfig` (0 errors), compiled with the real JSX compiler (`transformJSX`) and mounted in happy-dom; typing into the input filters the list.

items.what: `.value` on every ref read and write

items.instead: TSX: `<Show>`, `<For by>`, `value` plus `onInput`, ordinary props and handlers.

pickTheOther.title: When to pick Vue
items: You like single-file components with templates and scoped styles.
You depend on Nuxt modules or the wider Vue ecosystem.
Raw DOM speed is your only criterion: Vue 3.6 Vapor (RC) ties Pyreon on most row-board operations.
You hydrate very large keyed tables: Vue was marginally faster there (1.01×, one of two runs).

migrate.title: Keep your composables while you move.
migrate.text: `@pyreon/vue-compat` runs `ref`, `reactive`, `computed`, `watch`, lifecycle hooks and `provide`/`inject` on Pyreon. Templates move to TSX.
